summary: Laser and light-based devices used for visible blood vessels, redness and pigment concerns.
leadAnswer: Vascular / Pigment Laser covers the light-based devices Kaiteki uses on visible blood vessels, facial redness and pigment: Pro Yellow, M22 IPL and the dedicated DermaV platform. Which one a doctor uses depends on whether the target is a vessel or a pigment, and how deep it sits, which is decided at examination.
seoDescription: Laser treatment in Malaysia for pigmentation, redness and visible vessels using M22 IPL, Pro Yellow and DermaV. Book a free consultation at Kaiteki.
bringToConsult: Suitability also depends on which of the three devices is being considered, so bring your full medical and skincare history. With rosacea, mention your triggers, current treatment and any previous vascular laser.

avoidIf.body: in the area to be treated.
including oral isotretinoin and certain antibiotics.

avoidIf.lead: A history of keloid scarring or a light-sensitive condition.

sessionSteps.title: Consultation and assessment
sessionSteps.body: Your first visit is a consultation, not a treatment. The doctor examines whether the target is a vessel or a pigment, and how deep it sits, before choosing a device.

sessionSteps.title: A test area, where useful
sessionSteps.body: A patch or test area may be done before treatment goes ahead.

sessionSteps.title: The treatment
sessionSteps.body: The skin is cleansed, eye protection is fitted and the light is applied. Most people describe each pulse as a brief hot pinprick or warm snap.

afterSession.intro: Downtime is usually limited. Temporary redness or mild sensitivity typically settles. Use sun protection and gentle skincare afterwards.

bands.title: The first day or two
bands.body: Redness, warmth and mild swelling are common. Treated vessels can look temporarily darker or greyish, and treated pigment can darken or crust slightly before flaking away.

afterSession.aftercare: Use daily sun protection, keep skincare gentle, and avoid heat such as saunas and hot showers for as long as your doctor specifies.

risks.intro: Temporary effects can include redness, swelling or changes in pigmentation. Treating a vessel with a wavelength meant for pigment, or the reverse, is the mistake that causes the rest, and it is what the assessment and any test patch exist to prevent.
risks.common: Redness, swelling, bruising and small crusts over treated vessels.
risks.lessCommon: Blistering, burns, scarring and longer-lasting pigment change, more likely on unsuitable or recently tanned skin.
risks.pigmentNote: These devices are used across a range of skin tones, but some skin types and concerns need particular care to reduce the risk of pigment change, so your skin type and history are assessed first.
cannotDo: Vessels can recur, because the tendency behind them remains.
Rosacea and a tendency to flush are chronic: treatment addresses visible vessels, not the condition.
Very deep or large vessels may respond differently from fine superficial ones, and may need another approach.
risks.disclose: Tell your doctor about recent sun exposure and every medication you take.

costFactors.intro: Sessions and cost depend on the device, the concern and how your skin responds. The three platforms are not priced alike, so the cost follows the doctor's choice of device rather than preceding it.
factors: How extensive the concern is: a few discrete vessels, or diffuse redness.
Whether a chronic concern needs occasional maintenance sessions.

sections.heading: What is Vascular / Pigment Laser treatment?
body: Vascular / Pigment Laser is a group of light-based devices, not a single machine. Each wavelength is chosen to target either visible blood vessels or pigment in the skin. The group is commonly considered for facial redness and thread veins, sun spots and other pigment marks, and rosacea-associated flushing as part of a wider plan.
At Kaiteki the group is Pro Yellow (a QuadroStar 577nm yellow-light laser), M22 IPL (intense pulsed light) and the dedicated DermaV vascular-pigment platform.

sections.heading: How does one wavelength target a vessel and another a pigment?
body: Pro Yellow delivers 577nm yellow-light energy, a wavelength associated with absorption by blood vessels, and is generally considered for vascular concerns such as redness and visible vessels. M22 IPL delivers broad-spectrum light that can be filtered for either vascular or pigment targets, offering flexibility across different skin concerns in one platform.

The doctor selects the device, wavelength and settings for your concern and skin tone. The target, a vessel or a pigment particle, absorbs the energy, which may gradually reduce its visibility or prompt the body to clear it over time.

faqs.q: How is this different from DermaV?
faqs.a: DermaV is a dedicated dual-wavelength vascular-pigment device, used alongside Pro Yellow and M22 IPL.

faqs.q: Is this suitable for darker Asian skin tones?
faqs.a: These devices are used across a range of skin tones, but some skin types and concerns need particular care to reduce the risk of pigment change, so your skin type and history are assessed first.

faqs.q: How many sessions will I need?
faqs.a: A course of several sessions spaced a few weeks apart is common. Vessels can recur because the tendency behind them remains, so the doctor will say whether you are looking at a course or an ongoing arrangement.
Most people describe each pulse as a brief hot pinprick or warm snap. The devices cool the skin surface as they work, which is intended to keep sessions comfortable.

faqs.q: Is there downtime after laser for redness or pigmentation?
faqs.a: Usually little. Redness and mild swelling for a few hours to a day or two are common, and treated vessels or pigment can look temporarily darker before settling. Sun protection matters afterwards.
